question: Graded after the optimizer, does the krt-astar bundle (krt-grid connection router, then Freerouting's pull-tight of the changed area after each connection, then Freerouting's optimizer) leave fewer or more unrouted connections than the default bundle, split by region class (pin-field, open), on X01's five boards and four benchmark boards, without new clearance violations or vias in pads?
hypothesis: krt-astar completes fewer pin-field connections than the default on every board (preregistered in the X06 checklist; algorithms.md 'Grid A* followed by pull-tight')

default.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands X06, after P04's default-tree decision, in-process through freerouting-krt's harness (the CLI does not call freerouting_krt::register before C07)
default.command: X06_DSN={DSN} X06_SES={SES} X06_ALGO=freerouting-router cargo test --release -p freerouting-krt --test astar_bundle route_one_dsn -- --ignored --exact --nocapture

krt-astar.command: X06_DSN={DSN} X06_SES={SES} X06_ALGO=krt-astar cargo test --release -p freerouting-krt --test astar_bundle route_one_dsn -- --ignored --exact --nocapture

boards.x01: canary-pwr at canary 9511d9a and the KiCad 10.0.7 demos pic_programmer, interf_u, kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213 and video, prepared as X01 prepared them (tools/krt-h2h/prep_board.py: tracks and vias stripped, zones kept and refilled); the DSN is the one tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh exports from the prepared board ({DSN} of the arm command); canary-pwr's DSN is fixtures/canary-pwr/canary-pwr-9511d9a.dsn as in X01
boards.demo_dsns: the four exported demo DSNs' sha256 are added in an amendment before the first engine run (they depend on the prepared boards, as in X01)

eligibility: every board of both sets; a board where neither arm leaves a connection of a class unrouted is neutral for that class, printed; a board not graded (exit 2 of the grader, a crash, a timeout) fails that board for the arm that was not graded and is never a pass
region_classes: freerouting_krt::grid::regions (X06.2) on the input board the arms route (the DSN after the job's load sequence), before any run: pin-field when an end pad is fine-pitch (a pin of the same component within 0.65 mm centre to centre, or a pad side under 0.35 mm, or a component of at least 32 pins with a pitch of at most 0.8 mm; 1 um tolerance on both distances), open otherwise. If the operator amends X06.2's rule before the run, the amended rule is used and named in an amendment.

grading.x01_demos: tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh on the prepared board with the arm's command as ENGINE_COMMAND: the board's original rules, copper severities forced to error, the input board's DRC subtracted, KiCad 10.0.7; drc_real, kicad_unconnected and via_in_pad from the grader
grading.canary-pwr: the SES of each arm goes to the CANary layout session (canary-23) as in X01; until its grade exists canary-pwr counts as not graded for both arms: no win for either
grading.benchmark: the four x06-grid.txt fixtures have no .kicad_pcb in the repository: graded by Rust's DRC inside the harness (all_clearance_violations of the routed board; drc_new counts the violations with an item the run created) and its via-in-pad test
grading.region_split: on every board from the harness's region tally (route_one_dsn's printed RegionTally): the input board's connections of each class that are not complete on the routed board

metrics.name: drc_real
metrics.source: the KiCad grader on X01's demos; drc_new from Rust's DRC on the benchmark boards

metrics.name: unrouted_total
metrics.source: kicad_unconnected on the KiCad-graded boards, the routed board's airlines otherwise

metrics.name: raster_share
metrics.source: raster_share_on_a_set on the benchmark boards: window, raster and terminal cells against the grid search, per pass-1 connection on the input board; decides whether X04.6 (incremental stamps) is reopened

metric_definitions.unrouted_pin_field: connections of class pin-field on the input board whose two ends are not in one connected set on the routed board (regions::tally incomplete); unknown ends (no anchor left) are printed and not counted
metric_definitions.unrouted_total: printed beside the split: two input connections may share one remaining gap, so the split can sum to more than the total

keep_rule: krt-astar stays a selectable implementation only if, on one region class, it leaves fewer unrouted connections than the default on at least N-1 of the graded boards and on no board more, and on the other class it leaves no more than the default on any board; the hard metrics are 0 for krt-astar on every board. Otherwise X06.1's bundle code is removed (X05's krt-grid stage stays) and the numbers stay in X06.3's done note. Either way krt-astar is never a default from this run.
hypothesis_rule: the hypothesis holds if krt-astar's unrouted_pin_field is greater than the default's on every graded board; it fails otherwise, and the boards where it fails are printed

decision_table.keep: krt-astar stays selectable (off by default); X06.4 states the split and whether a hybrid (grid for open connections, the maze search for pin-field) is worth a checklist
decision_table.reject: the bundle code goes; X06.4 records the numbers and the hybrid verdict

stop_rule: one run per board and arm; no re-run except for a crash or a not-graded board, which is re-run once and reported
timing: the registered run waits for P04's default-tree decision (P00 README 'Order', Q00 README 'Order and critical path'); the X06 done notes give a pre-P04 dry run at the landing commit, labelled as such, not this registration's result
